places.action: Untick DHCP, keep the IPv4 address, subnet mask and default gateway as they are, and enter the Preferred DNS Server and the Alternate DNS Server below.

hikvisionWatch.router: Or have your router hand this camera 192.168.77.28 as its DNS server, with a DHCP reservation: OpenWrt, pfSense, OPNsense, MikroTik, ASUS and Pi-hole can do that for one device; UniFi, Synology and Firewalla only for a whole network (such as a separate one for the cameras); eero, Google/Nest Wifi, Deco and Orbi can’t, so change it on the camera. The router’s way works only while the camera takes its DNS from DHCP (automatic), and only from the camera’s next DHCP renewal or restart. Or block the camera’s internet in your router (see Keep this camera local). A DNS server from the router counts too, but it can change when the router renews the camera’s address.
hikvisionWatch.then: Then press Check again on the camera’s Security card.
warnings: Put Camera Bridge in both slots: with a public server, or none, as the second one, the camera can look names up without it.
If the camera asks to restart after you save, let it: it may keep its old DNS servers until then.
If the camera is plugged into a recorder’s own ports, the recorder runs its network: set its DNS on the recorder instead.
hikvisionWatch.why: The camera didn’t take the change.
